name: Toxic Blowpipe
shortDescription: The single most influential and contested ranged weapon in OSRS history.
summary: Released alongside Zulrah in 2015, the 2-tick rapid weapon shredded nearly every monster in the game for over six years before facing the historic 'Great Equipment Rebalance' nerf of 2021.

name: Zulrah
shortDescription: The Poison-Waste behemoth that forever altered OSRS PvM economics and boss design.
summary: Nicknamed the 'Money Snake', Zulrah's original 2015 drop table flooded the economy with skilling supplies and raw resources, leading to multiple drop table reductions and rotation updates.

name: Osmumten's Fang
shortDescription: The double-accuracy stab sword from Tombs of Amascut that outperformed specialized weapons.
summary: Originally blessed with reroll accuracy on both stab and slash, its unexpected dominance at bosses like Vardorvis and General Graardor forced Jagex to nerf its slash accuracy and invocation scaling outside ToA.

name: Voidwaker
shortDescription: The Wilderness Boss weapon whose 100% guaranteed magic damage spec shocked PvP and PvM.
summary: Assembled from pieces dropped by the reworked Wilderness bosses, its guaranteed-hit special attack triggered heated balance discussions across both the PvP and high-level PvM communities.

name: Abyssal Whip
shortDescription: The eternal classic weapon of RuneScape since 2005, serving as the benchmark for all melee gear.
summary: The backbone of OSRS melee combat since 2007. Later augmented with the Kraken Tentacle (2014) and cosmetic Volcanic/Frozen dyes from Bounty Hunter.

name: Dragon Claws
shortDescription: The iconic four-slice burst weapon revived from 2008 as a Chambers of Xeric raid reward.
summary: After failing early polls due to PTSD from 2008 Wyson/PvP rushing, Dragon Claws passed the Chambers of Xeric poll in late 2016 and returned as a premier raid reward.

name: Chambers of Xeric
shortDescription: OSRS's first raid, introducing the Great Olm, Twisted Bow, and team scaling mechanics.
summary: A monumental milestone that proved OSRS could create original large-scale endgame raids. Over 7 years, it saw major QoL updates including scouting overhauls, storage chests, and layout reworks.

name: Tombs of Amascut
shortDescription: The Egyptian-themed raid beneath the Kharidian Desert featuring customizable Invocations.
summary: ToA democratized raiding with its 0 to 600+ Raid Level system. Week 1 saw furious balancing passes on drop rates, potion mechanics, and Warden enrage phases.

name: The Inferno
shortDescription: The ultimate test of wave management, prayer flicking, and shield walking against TzKal-Zuk.
summary: Designed by Mod Kieren, The Inferno remained unbeaten for days until Woox achieved the world-first completion on June 3, 2017 without a Twisted Bow.

name: Great Kourend / Zeah
shortDescription: The massive new western continent that transformed from an empty square grid into a living fantasy realm.
summary: Infamously barren and square upon its 2016 launch, Kourend underwent landmark community-guided architectural overhauls inspired by player 'GentleTractor', culminating in the complete removal of the favor system in 2024.

name: Nightmare Zone (NMZ)
shortDescription: The dream-world minigame at the center of the infamous 6-hour AFK Guthan's & splashing debate.
summary: For nearly two years, players could sleep for 6 hours while Guthan's armor auto-retaliated max combat stats. In September 2015, Jagex introduced an auto-retaliate logout timer.

name: Revenant Caves
shortDescription: The high-risk Wilderness dungeon that sparked clan protection syndicates and multiple full reworks.
summary: From 100x statuettes day-1 money glitch to multi-combat protection clan cartels charging real money, the caves were overhauled into Singles-Plus with entrance fees.

name: Combat Achievements
shortDescription: Tiered mastery tasks across every boss in Gielinor that later transitioned to a point-based system.
summary: Originally requiring every single task in a tier to unlock rewards, Jagex overhauled the system into a flexible points-based threshold in 2023, unlocking huge accessibility.

name: Dinh's Bulwark
shortDescription: The massive raid shield at the heart of Wilderness tanking and PvP rebalance wars.
summary: Despised by PKers for making wildy agility and PvMers invulnerable to standard spellbooks, it saw multiple magic and melee defense stat swings before gaining defense-to-strength scaling.

name: Scythe of Vitur
shortDescription: The 3x3 multi-hit blood weapon from Theatre of Blood that rose, fell, and was resurrected.
summary: The pinnacle reward of ToB, the Scythe suffered from high upkeep blood rune costs and high defense boss metas until major accuracy and charge cost reductions restored its glory.

name: Tumeken's Shadow
shortDescription: The magic staff that multiplies equipped magic damage by 3x (4x in ToA), transforming the magic meta.
summary: Redefined endgame magic by tripling magic attack and magic damage bonuses, out-DPSing melee and ranged at high-defense bosses across the map.

name: Vorkath
shortDescription: The undead blue dragon of Ungael from Dragon Slayer II with consistent 3-4m/hr profit.
summary: Introduced with Dragon Slayer II, Vorkath became the new gold-standard for consistent solo bossing, with Ava's Assembler and dragon bolts reshaping ranged combat.

name: Serpentine Helm
shortDescription: The venom-inducing Zulrah helm that had its strength bonus removed, caused riots, and got it restored.
summary: In 2017, Jagex stripped its +5 strength bonus and venom on retaliation. After player backlash and the 2021 rebalance, strength bonus was partially restored.

name: Theatre of Blood
shortDescription: Lady Verzik Vitur's brutal Vampyre arena in Darkmeyer, celebrated as OSRS's tightest team PvM combat.
summary: Praised for its fluid dance mechanics at Verzik and Bloat, ToB later received Entry Mode (for Night at the Theatre quest) and Hard Mode with Holy/Sanguine ornaments.

name: Dragon Warhammer
shortDescription: The 30% defense-draining hammer with a 1/5,000 drop rate that drove Ironman players crazy for 8 years.
summary: Dropped by Lizardman Shamans, the DWH was a mandatory gatekeeper for endgame PvM until May 2024, when its drop rate was permanently boosted from 1/5000 to 1/3000.

name: 6-Hour AFK Splashing & NMZ
shortDescription: The defining controversy of early OSRS: getting 99 Magic and Melee while sleeping.
summary: By wearing full iron armor to achieve -68 Magic Attack and autocasting on chickens/rats in Lumbridge, players gained 6 hours of continuous XP while asleep until the September 2015 patch.

name: Black Chinchompa
shortDescription: The high-risk Wilderness explosive rodent that created the most contested hunting grounds in the game.
summary: Introduced in the Wilderness Rejuvenation, Black Chins allowed 250k+ Hunter XP/hr at the cost of being vulnerable to PKers in Level 33 Wilderness.

name: Twisted Bow
shortDescription: The Chambers of Xeric megarare whose damage and accuracy scale with the opponent's Magic level.
summary: The ultimate ranged endgame trophy. Its unique magic-scaling algorithm made it dominant at Commander Zilyana, Dagannoth Prime, and Olm, and it was involved in the legendary Feb 2019 'T-Bow Bush' server rollback.

name: Bow of Faerdhinen (BowFa)
shortDescription: The crystal bow crafted from Enhanced Crystal Weapon Seeds that inherited the high-defense ranged meta.
summary: Introduced in the Great Equipment Rebalance of 2021 alongside Crystal Armour buffs to bridge the massive gap between the nerfed Blowpipe and the ultra-rare Twisted Bow.

name: Occult Necklace
shortDescription: The 93 Slayer neckpiece that held an uncontested +10% Magic Damage for 10 years before the 2024 Magic Rebalance.
summary: Costing under 1 million GP from Thermonuclear Smoke Devils, the Occult single-handedly provided more magic damage than full Ancestral robes until Project Rebalance redistributed magic strength across armor pieces in May 2024.

name: Corporeal Beast
shortDescription: The massive Spirit Beast lurking in the Wilderness cave, guarding the Elysian Spirit Shield.
summary: Voted into OSRS in 2014, Corp introduced the Spirit Shields and sparked the famous 'spec-tabbing' POH pool meta using Dragon Warhammers, Bandos Godswords, and Arclight.

name: Coin Pouches & Auto-Clicking Fix
shortDescription: The Ardougne Knight inventory stacking pouch introduced to combat automated thieving macroers.
summary: To prevent players from remapping left-click and using foot pedals or autoclickers for 10 hours straight on Ardy Knights, Jagex introduced coin pouches that require manual opening.

name: Fortis Colosseum
shortDescription: Varlamore's high-octane 12-wave challenge rewarding Dizana's Quiver and Sunfire splinters.
summary: The premier ranged cape challenge succeeding the Inferno, featuring dynamic modifier curses per wave and Sol Heredit's sun beam mechanic.
